assessment: This is a thorough study showing that long-range correlations in the brain can arise without common input drive or long-range anatomical connections. These long-range correlations are modulated by the animal's behavioral state, a surprising finding that suggests a computational role for control of this kind of correlation. The paper details some analytical methods for modeling this behavior in disordered systems. The work will be of broad interest to neuroscientists, computational biologists, and biophysicists.
